docs.title: vexy-mkdocs-text-export
docs.text:
vexy-mkdocs-text-export is an MkDocs plugin. While MkDocs builds your site, it writes a plain-text (.txt) or Markdown (.md) copy of every page into the same folder as the page's .html file, and adds a link to that copy in the HTML.

Use the text copies to index a site for search, feed its content to a language model or a text-processing script, or move the content to another system.

docs.title: What goes in and what comes out
docs.text:
The plugin works on the finished HTML of each page, after MkDocs and every other plugin have rendered it.

Take a site with this source file:

docs/guide/setup.md

With the default settings, mkdocs build writes:

site/guide/setup/index.html   # the normal page
site/guide/setup/setup.txt    # the plain-text copy

The text file is named after the source Markdown file (setup.md becomes setup.txt), not after the HTML file. The plugin also adds this element to the <head> of index.html, so tools can find the copy:

<link href="setup.txt" rel="alternate" title="Text export"/>

Set markdown: true and the copy becomes setup.md, with links, emphasis and tables kept as Markdown.

docs.title: How the conversion works
docs.text:
1. MkDocs renders the page to HTML.
  2. The plugin passes the whole HTML document to html22text, which removes the tags you list in kill_tags and converts the rest with html2text.
  3. The plugin writes the result next to the page.
  4. A theme handler inserts a link to the result into the page HTML. The link is a hidden <link rel="alternate"> for most themes, and a visible button or link for material and cinder.

The plugin converts the whole HTML document, so site navigation, headers and footers also end up in the text unless you remove them with kill_tags. See Output format for details.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: install the plugin from PyPI or from source.
  • Quick start: add the plugin to a site and check the result.
  • Configuration: every option, its default and its effect.
  • Output format: what plain-text and Markdown output look like.
  • Theme handlers: how the link is added, and how to write your own handler.
  • Troubleshooting: common problems and their causes.

docs.title: License
docs.text: MIT. Its html22text dependency is also MIT-licensed.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page describes how the plugin is put together, for readers who want to change it or debug it.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
Path Role mkdocs_text_export_plugin/plugin.py MdTxtExportPlugin, the MkDocs plugin class. Reads the options and handles the build events. mkdocs_text_export_plugin/renderer.py Renderer. Maps the options onto html22text, writes the text files and loads the theme handler. mkdocs_text_export_plugin/themes/ Built-in theme handlers: generic, mkdocs, material, cinder, basictheme. mkdocs_text_export_plugin/__version__.py Written by hatch-vcs at build time. Not in git.

MkDocs finds the plugin through this entry point in pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."mkdocs.plugins"]
text-export = "mkdocs_text_export_plugin.plugin:MdTxtExportPlugin"

docs.title: Build events
docs.text: MdTxtExportPlugin uses four MkDocs events, in this order.

docs.title: on_config
docs.text:
1. If enabled_if_env is set and the named environment variable is not "1", the plugin sets self.enabled = False, prints a message and returns. Every later event checks self.enabled and returns straight away.
  2. If markdown is true, the output extension becomes md; otherwise it stays txt.
  3. The plugin logger level becomes DEBUG with verbose: true, else ERROR.

docs.title: on_nav
docs.text:
The plugin imports Renderer here, not at module level, so a disabled plugin never imports BeautifulSoup or html2text. It creates one Renderer with the theme name and the conversion options, and records the URL of every page in navigation order.

Renderer loads the theme handler at this point (see Theme handlers).

docs.title: on_post_page
docs.text:
MkDocs calls this once per page with the final HTML. For each page the plugin:

  1. Takes the page's output path (page.file.abs_dest_path) and source path (page.file.src_path).
  2. Builds the text file name from the source file name: setup.md gives setup.txt or setup.md.
  3. Builds a base_url from the output folder and the file name. html22text uses it to turn relative image and stylesheet URLs into absolute ones.
  4. Calls Renderer.write_txt(), which converts the HTML and writes the file.
  5. Calls Renderer.add_link(), which passes the HTML and the file name to the theme handler's modify_html().
  6. Returns the changed HTML to MkDocs.

If step 4 or 5 raises an exception, the plugin logs Error converting <source path> to text: <error>, counts the error and returns the HTML it received. The build continues.

docs.title: on_post_build
docs.text: Logs the number of converted files and the time taken at INFO level, and, if any page failed, <n> conversion errors occurred (see above) at ERROR level.

docs.title: The conversion
docs.text:
Renderer.render_doc() calls html22text() with these arguments:

html22text argument Value html_content The page HTML markdown The markdown option base_url Built in on_post_page open_quote, close_quote The options of the same name default_image_alt The default_image_alt option kill_strikethrough The hide_strikethrough option kill_tags The kill_tags list joined with commas file_ext_override md in Markdown mode, else empty

html22text then:

  1. Parses the HTML with BeautifulSoup.
  2. In Markdown mode, rewrites relative .html/.htm links to the output extension, and makes src and <link href> URLs absolute against base_url.
  3. Replaces every <mark> and <kbd> element with its text.
  4. Removes every element that matches a kill_tags selector.
  5. Converts the result with html2text.HTML2Text, with line wrapping turned off and mode-specific settings for emphasis, links, images and tables.

The plain_tables option is stored on the Renderer but not passed to html22text, so it has no effect.

docs.title: The html22text dependency
docs.text:
html22text is a separate MIT-licensed package by the same author, published on PyPI from https://github.com/twardoch/html22text. The plugin requires html22text>=1.0.1 and imports its html22text() function in mkdocs_text_export_plugin/renderer.py.

The source at tag v1.0.2 bundled a copy of html22text in mkdocs_text_export_plugin/_vendor/, because html22text was not yet on PyPI and PyPI rejects packages that depend on a git+https URL. Version 1.0.2 was never uploaded to PyPI, and the bundled copy has been removed.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure the plugin under the text-export key in the plugins list of mkdocs.yml. Every option is optional. This block lists all options with their default values:

plugins:
  - text-export:
      markdown: false
      kill_tags: []
      open_quote: "“"
      close_quote: "”"
      default_image_alt: ""
      hide_strikethrough: false
      plain_tables: false
      theme_handler_path: ""
      enabled_if_env: null
      verbose: false

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Effect markdown bool false Write Markdown (.md) instead of plain text (.txt). kill_tags list of str [] CSS selectors. Matching elements and their content are removed before conversion. open_quote str “ Text written in place of an opening <q> tag. close_quote str ” Text written in place of a closing </q> tag. default_image_alt str "" Markdown mode only: text used as the alt text of images that have none. hide_strikethrough bool false Passed to html2text. Has no visible effect on MkDocs output; see below. plain_tables bool false Accepted but not used; see below. theme_handler_path str "" Path to a Python file that adds the link to the text file. See Theme handlers. enabled_if_env str null Name of an environment variable. The plugin runs only when that variable equals 1. verbose bool false Set the plugin's log level to DEBUG instead of ERROR.

docs.title: markdown
docs.text:
With markdown: false (the default), the plugin writes <name>.txt. With markdown: true, it writes <name>.md, where <name> is the source file name without its extension.

The two modes differ in what they keep:

Element Plain text Markdown Bold and italic Markers removed **bold**, _italic_ Links Link text only [text](<url>), with .html targets changed to .md Images Removed ![alt](absolute path) Tables Pipe-separated rows Padded Markdown tables Code blocks Indented text Wrapped in [code] and [/code]

Output format shows real examples of both modes.

docs.title: kill_tags
docs.text:
A list of CSS selectors. Before the conversion, the plugin removes every element that matches one of them, together with its content. Plain tag names such as script or footer work, and so do class and attribute selectors such as .navbar or div[role=navigation].

plugins:
  - text-export:
      kill_tags:
        - script
        - style
        - .navbar
        - footer

The plugin converts the whole HTML document, not only the article, so kill_tags is how you keep navigation and footers out of the text.

docs.title: open_quote and close_quote
docs.text: html2text replaces inline quotations (<q>…</q>) with these two strings. With the defaults, <q>quoted</q> becomes “quoted”. Block quotes (<blockquote>) are not affected; they become lines that start with >.

docs.title: default_image_alt
docs.text: Only has an effect when markdown: true. An image without an alt attribute gets this text as its alt text, so <img src="a.png"> with default_image_alt: "image" becomes ![image](/…/a.png). In plain-text mode, images are removed completely, so the option does nothing there.

docs.title: hide_strikethrough
docs.text: The plugin passes this value to html2text as hide_strikethrough. html2text only applies that setting to Google Docs-style input, which this plugin does not enable. As a result, <del> and <s> content stays in the output in both modes, written as ~~text~~. To remove struck-through text, add del and s to kill_tags instead.

docs.title: plain_tables
docs.text: The plugin reads this option and stores it, but does not pass it on to the converter. Setting it has no effect on the output. Tables are always converted by html2text's own table handling.

docs.title: theme_handler_path
docs.text: A path to a Python file, resolved against the current working directory (the directory you run mkdocs from). The file replaces the built-in handler for your theme. If the file does not exist, the plugin prints a message and falls back to the built-in handler. See Theme handlers.

docs.title: enabled_if_env
docs.text:
When set, the plugin checks the named environment variable while MkDocs reads its configuration. If the variable is not exactly 1, the plugin prints a message and skips every later step:

Text export is disabled (set environment variable ENABLE_TEXT_EXPORT to 1 to enable)

When the option is not set, the plugin always runs.

docs.title: verbose
docs.text: Sets the level of the mkdocs_text_export_plugin.plugin logger to DEBUG. Without it, the level is ERROR, so only conversion errors are shown.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and enter it:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-text-export.git
cd vexy-mkdocs-text-export

  2. Create a virtual environment and install the package with its development tools (pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, mypy, mkdocs-material):

    uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
pytest -q
ruff check .
mypy mkdocs_text_export_plugin

The tests live in tests/:

File What it covers tests/test_plugin.py The plugin's build events and options tests/test_themes.py Every built-in theme handler and handler selection tests/test_integration.py A real mkdocs build that checks the text file and the injected link

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the tests on Python 3.12 and 3.13 on Linux and Windows, runs them again against MkDocs 1.5.x and 1.6.x, and runs ruff and mypy.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Every source file starts with a this_file: comment that gives its path.
  • The version comes from git tags through hatch-vcs. Do not add a version string to the code. mkdocs_text_export_plugin/__version__.py is generated and ignored by git.
  • Fix conversion bugs in html22text itself, release it, and raise the html22text>= floor in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Build the package and the documentation
docs.text:
The root build.sh builds either part or both:

./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only, into docs/
./build.sh package    # dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, then twine check

The documentation source is in src_docs/md/, and its configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. src_docs/build.sh builds it with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme in strict mode, so any warning fails the build. For a live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000:

src_docs/build.sh serve

Do not edit docs/ by hand. It is generated, and the Docs workflow rebuilds and commits it on every push to main that changes src_docs/.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
publish.sh makes a release:

  1. uvx gitnextver commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes both.
  2. ./build.sh package builds the wheel and the source distribution from that tag.
  3. uv publish dist/* uploads them to PyPI. It needs UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN or another uv publish credential.

Pushing the tag also starts .github/workflows/release.yml, which builds the package and creates a GitHub release with the matching CHANGELOG.md section. That workflow does not upload to PyPI.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later (requires-python = ">=3.12").
  • MkDocs 1.5.0 or later.

The plugin also installs html22text 1.0.1 or later, which brings in html2text, beautifulsoup4 and fire.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
pip install vexy-mkdocs-text-export

With uv:

uv pip install vexy-mkdocs-text-export

Note

If PyPI does not list the package yet, install it from GitHub instead: pip install "git+https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-text-export".

To run a one-off build without installing anything into your environment:

uvx --with vexy-mkdocs-text-export mkdocs build

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-text-export.git
cd vexy-mkdocs-text-export

  2. Install the package in editable mode, with the development tools:

    uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

The package version comes from the latest vX.Y.Z git tag (through hatch-vcs). A clone without tags gets a development version string.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
MkDocs finds the plugin through the mkdocs.plugins entry point named text-export. To confirm that the entry point is registered:

python -c "from importlib.metadata import entry_points; print(entry_points(group='mkdocs.plugins')['text-export'])"

The command prints:

EntryPoint(name='text-export', value='mkdocs_text_export_plugin.plugin:MdTxtExportPlugin', group='mkdocs.plugins')

To print the installed version:

python -c "import mkdocs_text_export_plugin as m; print(m.__version__)"

Next: Quick start.

docs.title: Output format
docs.text: This page shows what the plugin writes for one sample page, in both modes, and explains where each part of the output comes from.

docs.title: File names and locations
docs.text:
For each page in the navigation, the plugin writes one file into the folder that holds the page's HTML. The file name is the source file name with a new extension:

Source file HTML file (use_directory_urls: true) Text file docs/index.md site/index.html site/index.txt docs/guide/setup.md site/guide/setup/index.html site/guide/setup/setup.txt

With markdown: true, the extension is .md instead of .txt.

The plugin then adds a link to the text file into the HTML page. The link target is the bare file name (setup.txt), which works because both files sit in the same folder.

docs.title: Sample page
docs.text:
The examples below use this source file, docs/index.md:

# Welcome

This is **bold**, _italic_ and a [link to the guide](guide/setup.md).

> A short quote.

Inline <q>quoted</q> text and ~~gone~~ <del>deleted</del> text.

![Logo](logo.png)

| Name | Value |
|------|-------|
| a    | 1     |

The site uses the default mkdocs theme, and kill_tags removes the theme's navigation (.navbar, .col-md-3, .modal, footer).

docs.title: Plain-text output
docs.text:
site/index.txt:

# Welcome

This is bold, italic and a link to the guide.

> A short quote.

Inline “quoted” text and ~~gone~~ ~~deleted~~ text.

Name | Value  
---|---  
a | 1

In plain-text mode the plugin configures html2text to:

  • drop emphasis markers, so **bold** becomes bold;
  • keep link text and drop link targets;
  • remove images, including their alt text;
  • replace <q> with open_quote and close_quote;
  • write tables as pipe-separated rows without padding;
  • write list items with plain indentation and code blocks as indented text;
  • never wrap lines.

Headings still start with # and block quotes with >, because html2text writes those markers in every mode.

docs.title: Markdown output
docs.text:
With markdown: true, site/index.md contains (the image path is shortened):

# Welcome

This is **bold** , _italic_ and a [link to the guide](<guide/setup/>).

> A short quote.

Inline “quoted” text and ~~gone~~ ~~deleted~~ text.

![Logo](/…/site/logo.png)

| Name | Value |
|------|-------|
| a    | 1     |

In Markdown mode the plugin:

  • keeps bold (**) and italic (_) markers;
  • keeps links inline, wrapped in angle brackets: [text](<url>);
  • rewrites relative links that end in .html or .htm so they end in .md;
  • keeps images and turns their src into an absolute path, resolved against the page's location in the output folder on disk;
  • pads tables so the columns line up;
  • wraps code blocks in [code] and [/code] lines;
  • uses - for bullet list items.

Note

With use_directory_urls: true (the MkDocs default), MkDocs writes page links as folder URLs such as guide/setup/. Those links do not end in .html, so the .md rewrite does not apply to them.

Warning

Image paths in Markdown output point to the build machine's file system, for example /home/runner/work/site/logo.png. If you publish the .md files, rewrite those paths afterwards.

docs.title: Elements that become plain text
docs.text: In both modes, <mark> and <kbd> elements are replaced by their text, so <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> becomes Ctrl.

docs.title: Empty pages
docs.text: If a page converts to nothing but whitespace, the plugin writes an empty file.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page adds the plugin to an existing MkDocs site and checks the files it writes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An MkDocs site with a mkdocs.yml file and a docs/ folder.
  • The plugin installed in the same environment as MkDocs (see Installation).

docs.title: Add the plugin
docs.text:
1. Open mkdocs.yml.

  2. Add text-export to the plugins list. Put it last, so it sees the HTML after every other plugin has changed it:

    plugins:
  - search
  - text-export

    When you add a plugins list, MkDocs no longer enables search for you, so keep search in the list if you want it.

  3. Build the site:

    mkdocs build

MkDocs writes the site into site/, and the plugin adds one .txt file per page.

docs.title: Follow one page through the build
docs.text:
Say docs/index.md contains:

# Welcome

This is **bold**, _italic_ and a [link to the guide](guide/setup.md).

> A short quote.

| Name | Value |
|------|-------|
| a    | 1     |

After mkdocs build with the default mkdocs theme, site/index.txt contains this text, below the site navigation (shortened here):

# Welcome

This is bold, italic and a link to the guide.

> A short quote.

Name | Value  
---|---  
a | 1

What happened:

  • Bold and italic markers were dropped, because plain-text mode turns off emphasis.
  • The link kept its text and lost its URL.
  • Headings and block quotes kept their # and > markers. They come from html2text, which writes these even in plain-text mode.
  • The table became a pipe-separated table.

site/index.html now also contains <link href="index.txt" rel="alternate" title="Text export"/> in its <head>.

docs.title: Remove the site navigation from the text
docs.text:
The plugin converts the whole HTML document, so the theme's navigation bar, search dialog and footer appear in the text as well. Remove them with kill_tags, which takes CSS selectors:

plugins:
  - search
  - text-export:
      kill_tags:
        - .navbar
        - .col-md-3
        - .modal
        - footer

With these four selectors and the default mkdocs theme, site/index.txt starts directly with # Welcome. .navbar is the top bar, .col-md-3 the table-of-contents sidebar, .modal the search and keyboard-shortcut dialogs, and footer the page footer.

The selectors depend on the theme. For another theme, open one built .html file and look for the elements that wrap the navigation.

docs.title: Export Markdown instead
docs.text:
Set markdown: true:

plugins:
  - text-export:
      markdown: true

The plugin then writes index.md instead of index.txt, and keeps links, emphasis, images and tables as Markdown. See Output format.

docs.title: Export only in some builds
docs.text:
To export only when an environment variable is set, name the variable in enabled_if_env:

plugins:
  - text-export:
      enabled_if_env: ENABLE_TEXT_EXPORT

ENABLE_TEXT_EXPORT=1 mkdocs build   # writes the text files
mkdocs build                        # skips the export

When the variable is missing or not exactly 1, the plugin prints Text export is disabled (set environment variable ENABLE_TEXT_EXPORT to 1 to enable) and does nothing else.

docs.title: Theme handlers
docs.text: After the plugin writes a text file, it adds a link to that file into the page's HTML. A theme handler decides where the link goes. A theme with a content toolbar can show a visible button; a plain theme gets a hidden <head> link.

docs.title: Built-in handlers
docs.text:
The plugin picks a handler by the theme.name value in mkdocs.yml. It replaces hyphens in the name with underscores and looks for a module of that name in mkdocs_text_export_plugin/themes/.

theme.name Handler module What the handler adds mkdocs mkdocs <link href="…" rel="alternate" title="Text export"/> in <head> material material A download button inside <article class="md-content__inner md-typeset"> cinder cinder A small "Open text" link at the start of <footer> Any other name generic The same <head> link as mkdocs

When no module matches, the plugin prints a message such as Could not load theme handler readthedocs: No module named 'mkdocs_text_export_plugin.themes.readthedocs' and uses generic. The message is printed outside the MkDocs logger, so it does not count as a warning in mkdocs build --strict.

Note

The package also contains themes/basictheme.py, which adds the same head link. A theme named basic looks for themes/basic.py, does not find it, and ends up with generic, so the result is the same.

docs.title: The material button
docs.text:
The material handler inserts this element right after the opening <article class="md-content__inner md-typeset"> tag:

<a class="md-content__button md-icon" download href="index.txt" title="Text export"><svg …></svg></a>

It does a plain text replacement on that exact tag. A theme that is based on Material but writes the tag differently, or uses another theme name such as materialx, does not get the button. It gets the generic head link instead.

docs.title: The cinder link
docs.text: The cinder handler wraps an <a download class="txt-download">Open text</a> element in <small> and inserts it as the first child of the page <footer>. If the page has no <footer>, nothing is added.

docs.title: Write your own handler
docs.text:
A handler is a Python file with one required function:

def modify_html(html: str, href: str) -> str: ...
  • html is the full page HTML, after every other plugin has run.
  • href is the file name of the text copy, for example setup.txt.
  • The function returns the HTML that MkDocs will write.

Built-in handlers also define get_stylesheet() -> str, which returns CSS. The plugin never calls it, so a custom handler does not need it.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create a file in your project, for example text_link.py:

    from bs4 import BeautifulSoup


def modify_html(html: str, href: str) -> str:
    """Add a visible link to the text copy at the end of the main content."""
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
    main = soup.find("main") or soup.body
    if main is not None:
        p = soup.new_tag("p")
        a = soup.new_tag("a", href=href)
        a.string = "Plain-text version"
        p.append(a)
        main.append(p)
    return str(soup)

    beautifulsoup4 is already installed, because the plugin depends on it.

  2. Point theme_handler_path at the file:

    plugins:
  - text-export:
      theme_handler_path: text_link.py

  3. Run mkdocs build from the folder that contains text_link.py. The path is resolved against the current working directory, not against the location of mkdocs.yml.

Each built page now ends with a "Plain-text version" link.

docs.title: How a custom handler is loaded
docs.text:
The plugin loads the file with importlib when MkDocs builds the navigation.

  • If the file does not exist, the plugin prints Could not load theme handler <theme> from custom directory "<path>": … and uses the built-in handler for the theme.
  • Any other error in the file, such as a syntax error, is not caught and stops the build.
  • If modify_html raises an exception for a page, the plugin logs Error converting <page> to text: …, leaves that page's HTML unchanged and continues. The text file for that page has already been written at that point.

docs.title: No text files appear
docs.text:
Check these causes in order.

  1. The plugin is not in the plugins list. Run mkdocs build and look for .txt files next to the .html files in site/. If there are none, check that mkdocs.yml lists text-export under plugins.
  2. enabled_if_env is set. The build prints Text export is disabled (set environment variable <NAME> to 1 to enable). Set the variable to exactly 1: <NAME>=1 mkdocs build.
  3. You are looking for the wrong file name. The text file is named after the source file. docs/guide/setup.md produces site/guide/setup/setup.txt, not site/guide/setup/index.txt.

docs.title: The text contains the site menu, search dialog and footer
docs.text:
The plugin converts the whole HTML document. Remove the theme's navigation with kill_tags. For the default mkdocs theme:

plugins:
  - text-export:
      kill_tags: [.navbar, .col-md-3, .modal, footer]

For other themes, open a built .html file and pick selectors for the elements that wrap the menus. See Configuration.

docs.title: Could not load theme handler …
docs.text:
The build prints, for example:

Could not load theme handler readthedocs: No module named 'mkdocs_text_export_plugin.themes.readthedocs'

The plugin has no handler for your theme and uses the generic one, which adds a hidden <head> link. The text files are still written. To get a visible link, write a custom handler.

The message does not count as a warning, so mkdocs build --strict still succeeds.

docs.title: Could not load theme handler … from custom directory …
docs.text: The file named in theme_handler_path was not found. The path is resolved against the folder you run mkdocs from. Either run mkdocs from the project folder, or give a path that is correct from where you run it.

docs.title: Error converting <page> to text: …
docs.text:
The conversion or the theme handler raised an exception for that page. The page HTML is kept as it was, and the build goes on. At the end the build prints <n> conversion errors occurred (see above).

A common cause is a custom handler without a modify_html function:

Error converting index.md to text: module '.mkdocs' has no attribute 'modify_html'

docs.title: Struck-through text is still in the output
docs.text:
hide_strikethrough does not remove <del> or <s> content in MkDocs output. Add the tags to kill_tags:

plugins:
  - text-export:
      kill_tags: [del, s]

docs.title: plain_tables changes nothing
docs.text: The option is accepted but not used by the converter. Tables are always written in html2text's table format.

docs.title: Image paths in Markdown output point to my disk
docs.text: In Markdown mode, image URLs are made absolute against the page's output folder on the build machine. Rewrite them after the build if you publish the .md files.

docs.title: The Material download button is missing
docs.text: The material handler only runs when theme.name is material, and only finds its insertion point if the page contains <article class="md-content__inner md-typeset"> exactly. Other theme names, including materialx, get the hidden head link instead.
